promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Christian doctrine of the Trinity teaches that God is three persons in one. Which three persons make up the Trinity?
options: Father, Son and Holy Spirit
Father, Mother and Child
God, Jesus and Mary
Creation, Redemption and Salvation
questions.explain: The Trinity is the belief in one God who exists as three persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: Which term describes the Christian belief that God is all-powerful?
options: Omnipotent
Omniscient
Omnibenevolent
Transcendent
questions.explain: Omnipotent means all-powerful; omniscient means all-knowing and omnibenevolent means all-loving.

questions.q: According to Christian teaching, what is meant by 'original sin'?
options: The sinful human nature inherited by all people as a result of Adam and Eve's disobedience
The first sin a person personally commits in their life
A sin so serious that God cannot forgive it
The sin of rejecting Jesus as saviour
questions.explain: Original sin is the flawed human nature Christians believe was passed on to humanity through Adam and Eve's disobedience in Eden.

questions.q: The Christian belief in the incarnation refers to the idea that:
options: God became human in the person of Jesus
Jesus rose from the dead after his crucifixion
the soul is reborn into a new body after death
the bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ
questions.explain: The incarnation is the belief that God took on human form and 'became flesh' in Jesus Christ.

questions.q: In Christian belief, atonement is best understood as:
options: the restoring of the relationship between God and humanity through Jesus' death
the forgiveness of sins granted through baptism
the belief that Jesus was fully human as well as fully God
the final judgement of every human soul
questions.explain: Atonement means Jesus' death reconciled ('made at one') humanity with God, overcoming the separation caused by sin.

questions.q: On which day do Christians celebrate the resurrection of Jesus?
options: Easter Sunday
Good Friday
Christmas Day
Pentecost
questions.explain: The resurrection is celebrated on Easter Sunday; Good Friday marks the crucifixion and Pentecost the coming of the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: To describe God as 'just' means that God:
options: judges people fairly and rightly
loves everyone unconditionally
knows all things past and future
exists outside of time and space
questions.explain: God being just means he acts and judges with perfect fairness, rewarding good and punishing wrong.

questions.q: A Christian says, 'I cannot earn my place in heaven; I am saved only through God's undeserved gift.' This belief is best described as salvation by:
options: grace
law
works
wealth
questions.explain: Salvation by grace is the belief that eternal life is a free, unearned gift from God rather than something achieved by human effort.

questions.q: In the Roman Catholic Church, marriage is regarded as:
options: a sacrament
a contract that can be ended whenever the couple wish
a purely legal agreement with no religious meaning
an optional ceremony of no spiritual importance
questions.explain: Catholics view marriage as a sacrament, an outward sign of God's grace and a lifelong, sacred bond.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a purpose of marriage in Christian teaching?
options: To provide a faithful, lifelong union for companionship and the raising of children
To gain a financial advantage over other families
To secure a higher position in society
To allow a trial period before making any commitment
questions.explain: Christian teaching sees marriage as a lifelong, faithful union for love, companionship and the procreation and nurture of children.

questions.q: What is the official teaching of the Roman Catholic Church on the use of artificial contraception?
options: It is not permitted
It is actively encouraged for all couples
It is required before marriage
It is a matter of no moral concern
questions.explain: Following teachings such as Humanae Vitae, the Catholic Church teaches that artificial contraception is not permitted.

questions.q: Some Christians, such as many in the Church of England, may accept divorce because they believe:
options: marriage is a lifelong ideal, but forgiveness and a fresh start are sometimes needed
marriage vows carry no real importance
God is not concerned with human relationships
divorce should always be encouraged over reconciliation
questions.explain: While upholding marriage as lifelong, many Christians accept that God's forgiveness allows divorce and sometimes remarriage when a relationship has broken down.

questions.q: A married Christian couple choose natural family planning to space out having children. Which statement best reflects why some Christians prefer this method?
options: It works with the body's natural cycle rather than using artificial means
It guarantees the couple will never have any children
It is required by every Christian denomination
It is regarded as a form of abortion
questions.explain: Natural family planning is accepted by some Christians, including Catholics, because it avoids artificial methods and works with the body's natural fertility cycle.

questions.q: The Genesis teaching 'male and female he created them' is often used by Christians to support the belief that:
options: men and women are equal in the eyes of God
men should always be the head of the household
women should not work outside the home
marriage between men and women is unnecessary
questions.explain: Many Christians use this verse to argue that men and women, both made in God's image, have equal value and dignity.

questions.q: The 'sanctity of life' is the belief that:
options: life is holy and sacred because it is given by God
life only has value if a person is happy
human life is no more valuable than animal life
life should be preserved only when it is affordable
questions.explain: Sanctity of life is the belief that human life is sacred and God-given, and therefore should be respected and protected.

questions.q: The Roman Catholic Church generally opposes abortion because it teaches that:
options: life begins at conception and is sacred
abortion is entirely the mother's free choice
human life only begins at the moment of birth
abortion is acceptable in every circumstance
questions.explain: The Catholic Church teaches that life begins at conception, so abortion is seen as the taking of an innocent, sacred human life.

questions.q: Euthanasia is best defined as:
options: the painless killing of someone to relieve their suffering
the natural process of dying from old age
the medical care of the dying within a hospice
the refusal of all forms of medical treatment
questions.explain: Euthanasia is the deliberate, painless ending of a person's life, usually to relieve suffering from an incurable condition.

questions.q: In Christianity, the principle of 'stewardship' teaches that humans should:
options: care for and protect the world on God's behalf
use the earth's resources however they wish
worship nature itself as divine
avoid all contact with the natural world
questions.explain: Stewardship is the belief that God has given humans responsibility to look after and protect the created world.

questions.q: A Christian argues that only God has the right to decide when a person dies, so euthanasia is wrong. This argument is most directly based on:
options: the sanctity of life
the quality of life
the right to personal autonomy
the theory of evolution
questions.explain: The claim that life is God-given and only God may end it is an application of the sanctity of life principle.

questions.q: A person in severe pain asks a doctor to end their life, arguing that their suffering has made life no longer worth living. This appeal is based most directly on which principle?
options: quality of life
sanctity of life
stewardship
original sin
questions.explain: The argument that suffering makes a life no longer worth living is based on the quality of life, which contrasts with the sanctity of life view.
